Figure 3: how closely a mortality-based targeting rule tracks the effect-based
gold standard, under the primary (linear treatment-by-space interaction) model.
The x-axis is the cumulative share of all doses delivered as villages are added
in each rule's rank order; the y-axis is the predicted deaths averted, as a % of
the universal-treatment total. The inset table gives the targeting-curve area
ratio ("heterogeneity captured") for each mortality aggregation level. Every
object plotted here is built in `07-targeting-analysis.qmd` and read back from
`data/targeting_fig3_objects.rda`; this script attaches no model, so it stays a
pure presentation layer.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

rm(list = ls())
```

```{r Load packages and config}

library(here)
library(tidyverse)

source(here::here("analysis", "0-config.R"))
```

```{r Load data}

# The Figure 3 hand-off bundle: point-estimate targeting curves, the block-rule
# knots, the concordance and targeting-curve area-ratio tables, the rule
# colours/labels, and a metadata list. See the save chunk at the end of 07 for
# what each object carries.
#
# base::load(), not bare load(): 0-config.R attaches renv, whose load() (open a
# project) masks base R's load() (restore an .rda). The qualifier dodges the mask.
base::load(here("data", "targeting_fig3_objects.rda"))

# The primary specification, named by 07 rather than hard-coded here, so this
# figure cannot drift from the model the analysis calls primary.
ref_key     <- fig3_meta$ref_key
ref_display <- fig3_meta$ref_display
```

```{r prep data}

# Single panel: filter the multi-model objects to the primary specification and
# restore the rule factor order so colours, legend and annotation rows all read
# in the same sequence as everywhere else in the analysis.
rule_order <- names(rule_labels)

curves_plot <- curves %>%
  dplyr::filter(model == ref_key) %>%
  mutate(rule = factor(rule, levels = rule_order))

block_knots_ref <- block_knots %>%
  dplyr::filter(model == ref_key) %>%
  mutate(rule = factor(rule, levels = rule_order))

# `random` carries a zero-height band (a single knot at (1, 1) in every draw), so
# it is excluded from the ribbon layer deliberately rather than by oversight -
# drawing it would invite reading its invisible band as merely too narrow to see.
band_rules <- c("rd", "mort_grappe", "mort_csi", "mort_dept")
# ribbon_dat <- curves_plot %>% dplyr::filter(rule %in% band_rules)

rule_labels["random"] <- "Random"
rule_labels["rd"] <- "ATE-based ranking (reference)"

# Linetypes: the two reference curves (RD envelope, random) are the only ones in
# the line legend; the three mortality curves are identified by the coloured
# inset table instead. Solid RD, dashed random.
# NOTE: the original `rule_lt` definition was lost when this file was overwritten;
# this is a reconstruction - adjust if your linetypes differed.
rule_lt <- c(rd = "solid", mort_grappe = "solid", mort_csi = "solid",
             mort_dept = "solid", random = "dashed")
```

```{r annotation layout}

# The annotation block sits in the top-left, above everything the curves and their
# bands reach in that corner. Measuring headroom on the ribbon's UPPER edge rather
# than the point-estimate line keeps the band from sliding behind the text unseen.
annot_x       <- 0.02
annot_step    <- 0.07
annot_x_right <- 0.16   # right edge of the annotation column, on the coverage axis
annot_pad     <- 0.05   # clearance between the highest band and the lowest text row

annot_headroom <- curves_plot %>%
  dplyr::filter(x <= annot_x_right) %>%
  summarise(v = max(prop_averted, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(v)

n_annot_rows <- length(band_rules)
annot_bottom <- annot_headroom + annot_pad
annot_top    <- annot_bottom + n_annot_rows * annot_step

# One targeting-curve area ratio per informative rule, coloured to match its
# curve. `random` is dropped (0 by construction). The area ratio is the share of
# the achievable above-45-degree benefit-area a rule retains: the magnitude-
# weighted quantity the eye actually reads off the figure, so it is what the
# annotation reports. `rd` reads 1.00 as the envelope.
area_annot <- area_ratio_tab %>%
  dplyr::filter(model == ref_key, rule != "random") %>%
  dplyr::filter(model == ref_key, rule != "rd") %>%
  mutate(rule = factor(rule, levels = rule_order)) %>%
  arrange(rule) %>%
  mutate(x = annot_x,
         y = annot_top - annot_step * dplyr::row_number(),
         label = sprintf("%.1f%%", area_ratio * 100))

table_data <- area_annot %>%
  dplyr::select(rule, label) %>%
  mutate(rule = as.character(rule)) %>%
  mutate(row_colour = rule_colours[rule]) %>%
  mutate(rule = dplyr::case_when(
    rule == "mort_grappe" ~ "Village-level",
    rule == "mort_csi" ~ "CSI-level",
    rule == "mort_dept" ~ "Department-level",
    TRUE ~ rule
  )) %>%
  dplyr::rename(`Mortality\naggregation level` = rule, `Heterogeneity\ncaptured` = label)

row_colours <- table_data$row_colour
table_data  <- dplyr::select(table_data, -row_colour)

# Convert to a tableGrob (grid graphics object)
table_grob <- gridExtra::tableGrob(
  table_data, rows = NULL,
  theme = gridExtra::ttheme_minimal(
    base_size = 10,
    core = list(
      bg_params = list(
        # gridExtra fills the cell matrix column-major, so repeat the
        # per-row pattern once per column to get a full-row fill
        fill  = rep(row_colours, times = ncol(table_data)),
        alpha = 0.35,     # keep text legible over the colour
        col   = NA
      ),
      fg_params = list(col = "black")
    ),
    colhead = list(fg_params = list(fontface = "bold"))
  )
)
```

```{r figure 3}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6.5

pl3 <- ggplot(curves_plot,
               aes(x = x, y = prop_averted, colour = rule, group = rule)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = rule), linewidth = 1) +
  # show.legend = FALSE: without it this layer stamps a point glyph onto every
  # legend key, including the three rules that contribute no block knots.
  geom_point(data = block_knots_ref, size = 1.6, alpha = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Doses delivered (% of universal-treatment doses)",
                     breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.1),
                     labels = seq(0, 100, 10)) +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Predicted deaths averted (% of universal-treatment total)",
                     breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.1),
                     labels = seq(0, 100, 10)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = rule_colours, labels = rule_labels[c("rd", "random")], name = NULL, breaks = c("rd", "random")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = rule_lt, breaks = c("rd", "random"), labels = rule_labels[c("rd", "random")], name = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
        legend.box.just = "center",
        legend.justification.inside = "center",
        legend.key.justification = "center",
        legend.text = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        legend.position = "inside",
        legend.position.inside = c(0.7, 0.12)) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(keywidth = unit(1, "cm")),
         linetype = guide_legend(keywidth = unit(1, "cm")))

fig3 <- pl3 + coord_equal() +
  inset_element(table_grob,
                  left = 0.5, bottom = 0.2,
                  right = 0.9, top = 0.45)

fig3

ggsave(here("results", "manuscript", "fig3-targeting_curves.png"),
       plot = fig3, bg = "white", width = 7, height = 7.2, dpi = 300)

fig3_gr <- pl3  +
  coord_fixed(0.61803399) +
  inset_element(table_grob,
                left = 0.5, bottom = 0.2,
                right = 0.9, top = 0.45)

fig3_gr
```
